name: Government
description: Political systems, leadership structures, strengths, and tensions

fields.structure: A sovereign inherits rule through an established bloodline.
fields.leadership: Monarch advised by ministers and powerful families.
fields.strength: Clear succession and fast centralized decisions.
fields.tension: An unsuitable heir and rival branches threaten civil war.

fields.structure: The crown exchanges land and privilege for military service.
fields.leadership: Monarch above semi-independent dukes, counts, and knights.
fields.strength: Local defense and administration need little central bureaucracy.
fields.tension: Great vassals obey selectively and maintain private armies.

fields.structure: Districts or communities elect representatives for fixed terms.
fields.leadership: Council selects a speaker with limited executive authority.
fields.strength: Broad participation and peaceful replacement of leaders.
fields.tension: Slow compromise leaves urgent problems unanswered.

fields.structure: Property-holding guilds and trading families elect magistrates.
fields.leadership: A doge or first consul checked by commercial councils.
fields.strength: Strong finance, diplomacy, infrastructure, and trade.
fields.tension: Poor citizens have little voice and corruption is normalized.

fields.structure: Autonomous clans unite for war, migration, and shared law.
fields.leadership: Clan chiefs meet under a chosen high speaker.
fields.strength: Flexible local rule and strong personal obligations.
fields.tension: Old feuds and disputed grazing rights fracture consensus.

fields.structure: Religious law and civil authority are formally identical.
fields.leadership: High priesthood interprets doctrine and appoints administrators.
fields.strength: Shared purpose, welfare institutions, and moral legitimacy.
fields.tension: Doctrinal disagreement is treated as political treason.

fields.structure: Senior officers govern through emergency decrees and regional commands.
fields.leadership: A council of generals chaired by a supreme commander.
fields.strength: Rapid mobilization, logistics, and crisis response.
fields.tension: Permanent emergency rule suppresses civilians and divides officers.

fields.structure: Recognized professional guilds hold seats according to economic importance.
fields.leadership: Guildmasters negotiate policy through a closed grand chamber.
fields.strength: Expert administration and investment in skilled production.
fields.tension: Unguilded workers and new industries are excluded.

fields.structure: A hereditary monarch shares authority with an elected assembly.
fields.leadership: Crown manages continuity while ministers require legislative support.
fields.strength: Combines symbolic unity with accountable government.
fields.tension: Neither side agrees where royal emergency powers end.

fields.structure: Citizens vote personally on laws in regular assemblies.
fields.leadership: Short-term elected officials execute public decisions.
fields.strength: High legitimacy and strong civic participation.
fields.tension: Citizenship exclusions and manipulation by wealthy speakers persist.

fields.structure: Political authority depends on recognized magical competence.
fields.leadership: A conclave of licensed master mages assigns civil offices.
fields.strength: Powerful public works and informed magical regulation.
fields.tension: Non-mages face exclusion and magical accidents lack oversight.

fields.structure: Each lineage appoints its oldest capable representative.
fields.leadership: Consensus council led by the most respected mediator.
fields.strength: Long memory and caution preserve stability.
fields.tension: Young people and recent arrivals cannot influence policy.

fields.structure: Eligible citizens are randomly selected for temporary public offices.
fields.leadership: Rotating committees supervised by permanent civil servants.
fields.strength: Difficult to capture through elections or hereditary privilege.
fields.tension: Inexperienced officials depend heavily on unelected administrators.

fields.structure: Two sovereigns from different peoples must approve major decisions.
fields.leadership: Separate courts joined by a shared chancellery.
fields.strength: Protects the autonomy of both founding populations.
fields.tension: Routine disputes can paralyze the entire state.

fields.structure: Independent cities share defense, currency, and foreign policy.
fields.leadership: Delegates meet in a congress with a rotating host city.
fields.strength: Local freedom backed by collective economic power.
fields.tension: Rich cities avoid burdens while dominating shared decisions.

fields.structure: Precedent and courts govern more strongly than elected lawmaking.
fields.leadership: A hierarchy of judges culminates in a supreme tribunal.
fields.strength: Predictable law and strong protection from arbitrary rulers.
fields.tension: Legal complexity empowers judges and excludes ordinary citizens.

fields.structure: Policy follows authenticated prophecies interpreted by civil officials.
fields.leadership: A regent governs until a predicted rightful ruler appears.
fields.strength: Long-term planning can anticipate otherwise invisible threats.
fields.tension: Competing interpretations justify repression and endless delay.

fields.structure: Dead rulers remain legally in office through ritual consultation.
fields.leadership: Living ministers interpret votes from preserved ancestral spirits.
fields.strength: Institutional memory literally survives each generation.
fields.tension: The dead resist change and ministers may falsify their wishes.

fields.structure: Authority transfers among four administrations with the seasons.
fields.leadership: Each seasonal court controls policy for three months.
fields.strength: Different priorities receive guaranteed recurring attention.
fields.tension: Long projects are sabotaged or reversed every transition.

fields.structure: A chartered company owns infrastructure and exercises public authority.
fields.leadership: An appointed governor answers to distant shareholders.
fields.strength: Efficient investment and rapid exploitation of resources.
fields.tension: Residents are treated as employees, debtors, or obstacles rather than citizens.
